{{Quote|Do you see that flying irid? Look at the yellow on the underside of its wings.''"<br />"''Beautiful.''"<br />"''Yes. But they are horrible birds. They attack their own kind. It's strange, though. They nurture their young with great care. They teach them to fly, to hunt, to nest. Yet when their young reach maturity they are just as likely to eat their parents as each other.|Tahl and Qui-Gon Jinn|<ref name="Death" />}}
'''Irids''' were flighted [[Bird/Legends|birds]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ragoon VI]]. With [[Color/Legends|yellow]] feathers on their wings,<ref name="CSWE" /> they were noted for plumage that was pleasing to the [[Eye/Legends|eye]]. Nevertheless, they were notorious for their violent behavior toward others of their [[Species/Legends|species]]. In contrast, they were quite nurturing to their young and taught them how to take care of themselves. Upon reaching maturity, when they developed that pugnacious disposition, offspring would often attack their own [[Parent/Legends|parents]] indiscriminately. Two [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Tahl]], saw an irid while visiting Ragoon VI for a [[Jedi training/Legends|training]] mission in the wake of Jinn's [[Padawan/Legends|apprentice]], [[Xanatos]], turning to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]<ref name="Death" /> around [[53 BBY/Legends|53 BBY]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places the [[Telosian Civil War]], soon after which Xanatos turned, in this year.</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
An irid appeared in a flashback from the fifteenth novel of the [[Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice|''Jedi Apprentice'']] young readers series, [[2001]]'s ''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Death of Hope]]'', by [[Jude Watson]].<ref name="Death" />
